model_annotation: This donut chart visually represents two categorical distributions: “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” and “Max Ambiguity (Inner)”, each depicted as concentric rings. The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer)”, is divided into four segments with varying shades of blue, representing standard deviation values (Std: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94), and their respective proportions are 49.0%, 47.7%, 7.0%, and 5.0%. The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner)”, is divided into three segments with lighter shades of blue, representing maximum ambiguity values (Max: 1, 2, 3), with proportions of 38.0%, 39.0%, and 14.2%. Each segment is clearly labeled with its percentage value inside the ring, and a legend on the right side of the chart provides a color-to-value mapping for both rings, with the outer ring using darker blues and the inner ring using progressively lighter blues. The chart is structured to show how the two distributions relate within the same circular space, with the outer ring’s segments appearing to be ordered in descending size from top-left to bottom-right, and the inner ring’s segments appearing to be ordered similarly.
